---
title: "Bayesian multilevel adjustment"
---

Bayesian methods are experimental on the integration branch. The tested
fixed-effect Poisson case matches R priors, likelihood and shared-draw predictions.
Its zero-bias counterfactual extrapolates far outside the observed bias range,
producing very large and imprecisely estimated posterior means. Backend agreement
and reliable corrected-flow estimates are separate questions.

Install `.[bayesian]` for Bambi/PyMC, or `.[latent]` and CmdStan for latent models.
The `backend` choices `rstanarm` and `brms` identify R model/prior conventions;
non-latent Python sampling runs through Bambi/PyMC.

```python
from debiaspy import adjust_multilevel_bayes, debiaspy_example_data

bundle = debiaspy_example_data(n_areas=5, complete_grid=True)
result = adjust_multilevel_bayes(
    bundle["mpd_od"], bundle["coverage"],
    covariates_df=bundle["covariates"], distance_df=bundle["distance"],
    model_engine="bayesian", random_intercept="none",
    mobility_formula="~ log_pop_o + log_pop_d + log_distance",
    bias_formula="~ bias_e_origin",
    iter=2000, chains=4, seed=20260710,
)
print(result.attrs["diagnostics"])
```

Inspect divergences, effective sample size and R-hat, alongside
`adjusted_flow_total` and `counterfactual_support`. A runtime warning is emitted
when the adjusted total mean's Monte Carlo standard error exceeds 5% of its
mean. The warning leaves the R-compatible mean estimator unchanged. Its absence
provides limited evidence about precision and does not establish model validity.

Random slopes, multiple/nested/crossed random effects and latent ZIP/ZINB require
further implementation. The full Bayesian sampling matrix and six retained
R-reference ZIP quality failures remain outstanding. Read the
[investigation](../development/bayesian-investigation.md) for evidence and
commands before interpreting the example's adjusted flows.
